chose: Scope embeds three truths, the spec model, the run records, and the journal records, and derives every view from them at render: latest verdicts, kept-from-earlier marks, reliance, open escalations, counts
over: embedding a precomputed status view and a precomputed reliance table beside the records
because: Data is destiny: store truth once and compute its consequences; two stored copies of the same fact are an invitation to disagreement, and the page must never show a verdict its records do not carry

chose: Every card id is prefixed by its view (component-, invariant-, reliance-, run-, journal-, and the glossary's coherence-/domain-) and a hash resolves to its view by that prefix, so one id space serves deep links across views
over: a hash syntax of view/id with a separator
because: the glossary's existing related links keep working unchanged, and a reader can paste any card id as a link without knowing which view holds it

chose: Reliance is computed from the latest chokepoint run entry's files, each mapped to the component whose folder is its longest prefix, with the owning component marked
over: waiting for the run record to carry per-site reference data before rendering reliance
because: the run record carries the definition and reference files today and that is enough to name components; what it lacks is said on the view rather than hidden behind an empty section

chose: The chokepoint grade ladder on the page is composed from the adapter's ladder (its top rung and because) plus fixed text for reference-choked, broken, and not chokeable, each rung naming who enforces it
over: hardcoding TypeScript's ladder in the view
because: the ladder is adapter-defined; a Python project must see its own top rung and its own enforcer

chose: The builder takes --root to build over another project: its spec tree, runs, journal, and glossary (located through the lifecycle's projectGlossaryPath) become the domain layer beneath Coherence's glossary
because: Mnemion is the first adopter and its data must render without a second code path; one loadState serves the page and the agent query alike

chose: The agent query answers from the same ShellState the page renders (loadState), with a fixed set of five questions and no query language
over: a query language over the model
because: the glossary's agent query concept fixes the questions first; a query language is refused until the fixed set proves insufficient

chose: The agent query gets its state through buildScopePage, the chokepoint that protects loadState, and drops the document it also renders
over: calling loadState directly from the query command
retiring the deterministic-build chokepoint so loadState becomes a shared seam
because: the edit hook revealed the direct call as a bypass (a structural defect on Scope's deterministic build); routing through the chokepoint keeps the invariant in force at the cost of reading the styles and browser sources once per query, which is milliseconds; a retirement is a human's to acknowledge, not mine

chose: The inline module refuses a top-level name declared in two browser sources, by name, at build time
over: relying on the check test to notice a page whose script fails to parse
because: joining the sources into one module gives them one name space; a duplicate function is a SyntaxError the browser reports to nobody, and the first build of the six views shipped exactly that until the bundle was run under node

chose: Relative imports are stripped from the browser sources by a multi-line regular expression over the whole module text
because: a view's import list spans several lines once it imports more than a few names, and the per-line filter left the import statement in the page, where it redeclared every name it imported

observation: Every verdict on Coherence's own invariants view carries the kept-from-an-earlier-run mark because the run the edit hook appends checks only the invariants an edit may touch
couldBe: the status view should treat the edit hook's partial runs as a different kind of run than a full pass
the mark is right and the full run at regulate will clear it
discriminatedBy: run a full pass and rebuild the page; if every mark clears, the mark is right and only the hook's partial runs made it look universal

what: enforcement.test.ts expects the hook's PostToolUse line to say run 2026-09-17, the date the test was written, so the whole suite goes red after midnight UTC
evidence: npm test at 2026-09-18T00:0x UTC: 'The input did not match the regular expression /... run 2026-09-17 .../. Input: run 2026-09-18'; the same file alone before midnight was green; src/enforcement is not this session's to edit
